major IMG-02 frontend/components/architect-2525/tiny-floorplan.tsx:88 — The whole-house 2D floor plan only renders real objects when `r.objects?.length` (line 88); with no saved objects it falls to the generic hand-drawn `furniture(r.k)` sketch (lines 91-96). But the 3D voxel/mini-map now renders `r.objects ?? defaultObjectsForRoom(r.k)` (voxel-house.tsx:251). Both whole-house views are displayed together on the Model tab (architect-design.tsx:367 TinyFloorplan + :372 VoxelHouse mini). So on first enter — before any edit commits objects — the 2D plan and the 3D voxel show DIFFERENT furniture, breaking the operator's IMG-02 words '2D room ⇄ voxel must always mirror.' The gate architect-product-truth.test.mjs:148 asserts the mirror by inspecting ONLY the voxel source, so it stays green while the 2D plan diverges. Fix: give tiny-floorplan the same fallback — draw placedContents(r.objects?.length ? r.objects : defaultObjectsForRoom(r.k)) when showFurniture.
major IMG-02 frontend/components/architect-2525/room-designer.tsx:121 — The IMG-02 one-finger-orbit hardening (`pan:false`) was applied only to voxel-house.tsx:43. The room-designer's own exploded 3D pane (voxel3D) builds its cameras from CAM_OPTS at room-designer.tsx:121 with `touchOrbit:true` but WITHOUT `pan:false`. For the exact failure the fix cites in its comment — a webview that mis-reports a touch as pointerType 'mouse' — the orbit predicate (use-rcore-gestures.ts:72) then falls through to PAN, so one finger pans instead of orbiting in the primary room-design 3D surface. Two sibling 3D surfaces now make different gesture promises, and the operator's own test device (the one whose mis-report motivated the fix) would still hit the original bug inside the room designer. Fix: add `pan:false` to room-designer CAM_OPTS so both 3D surfaces orbit on one finger.

major IMG-02 lib/room-objects.ts:417-435 (defaultObjectsForRoom) — The default-furniture packer wastes whole vertical bands, so the Master Bedroom (M) — the most-likely first room — still opens more than half empty: running defaultObjectsForRoom('M') yields only 4 of 9 (bed, nightstand, dresser, wardrobe); tv, chair, mirror, lamp, rug silently vanish, and Living (L) drops the rug. Cause: the bed's 6ft depth consumes the first row band, and the next wrap sets cy=ROOM_GRID (off-grid) so every later item is skipped. ThothFAIL · 106w
Data & Analytics
I counted what the layout math yields, not what the labels promise. defaultObjectsForRoom honours the replay law cleanly — no Math.random, stable iteration, unique ids, involutive mirror, zero overlap (0.000 ft²), every footprint in-bounds, gates green. But its shelf-packer is lossy: a six-foot bed claims the entire first row, the third row opens at cy=10, and a silent `continue` deletes the remainder. The Master Bedroom ships four of nine assets; five vanish — the operator's exact HOLD, on the flagship room, on a trust deadline. Worse, the one gate meant to catch this, `length===9 || length>0`, can never fail. Determinism without completeness is a precise lie.
blocker IMG-02 lib/room-objects.ts:422-433 (packer), rendered via room-designer.tsx:74 + voxel-house.tsx — defaultObjectsForRoom's grid packer silently drops default furniture, re-triggering the operator's exact HOLD ('default items vanish on room-enter') on the flagship room. defaultObjectsForRoom('M') returns only 4 of the 9 ROOM_ASSETS (bed,nightstand,dresser,wardrobe) and drops tv,chair,mirror,lamp,rug; defaultObjectsForRoom('L') drops rug (6 of 7). Cause: the bed's 6-ft depth sets rowD=6, so row 1 reserves 7 ft (6+GAP), row 2 starts at cy=7, row 3 at cy=10; then `if (cy + d > ROOM_GRID) continue` (line 428) discards every remaining item instead of gap-filling the small pieces (mirror d=0.2, tv d=0.4, lamp d=1) into existing rows. room-designer.tsx:74 (`room.objects ?? defaultObjectsForRoom(room.k)`) and the voxel render exactly this output, so on entering the Master Bedroom (lib/room-layout.ts:34, key 'M') on his phone 5 of 9 defaults are still missing — the HOLD is NOT cleared. Verified by running the function over all 9 room keys.
major IMG-02 tests/room-objects.test.mjs:239 — The gate meant to prove defaults derive fully from ROOM_ASSETS is tautological, which is why the dropped-items regression shipped unseen. The line `ok(dM.length === ROOM_ASSETS["M"].length || dM.length > 0, "defaults derive from the room's ROOM_ASSETS")` evaluates to `(4===9) || (4>0)` = `false || true` = true. The correct equality check is present but neutered by the `|| dM.length > 0` clause, so the suite stays green (130/130) while 5 of 9 items vanish. It should assert `defaultObjectsForRoom(rk).length === ROOM_ASSETS[rk].length` for every room key M/B/C/L/K/D/O/S/E, which currently fails for M and L.
minor IMG-02 lib/room-objects.ts:415-416 and room-designer.tsx:73 — Both comments claim the first edit 'commits the full set, so it persists', but commit() (room-designer.tsx:170) is always called with an op over `objects`, which is the 4-item packed default from line 74 — never the 9-item ROOM_ASSETS. So after the first tap/nudge the saved room holds 4 items and tv/chair/mirror/lamp/rug are gone permanently, not merely on initial view. The doc comment overstates what persists and masks finding #1.
ThorCONCERN · 124w
Risk & Security Stress
I stress-tested every throw, hang, and data-loss path and the restore boundary held: sanitizeObjects whitelists kind, clamps the grid, never crashes the renderers — good discipline. The add path guards null layers and empty drops; the gesture change leaves no stray setPan; the packer clamps every placement inside the room. No crash, no hang. But the shield has a seam. Empty a room and the two views split: the 2D plan honours the empty array while the voxel falls through to canned furn3d — the operator said ALWAYS mirror, and the code's own comment lies about it. Worse, that emptied state evaporates on reload because [] sanitizes to undefined, resurrecting defaults. An invariant breached is a breach. Close the seam before he touches it.
major IMG-02 components/architect-2525/voxel-house.tsx:149 — Mirror divergence on an emptied room. voxel-house.tsx:149 `opts.objects?.length ? objects3d(...) : (opts.furn && furn3d(...))` treats a 0-length objects array as "none" and reverts to the canned furn3d placeholder, while the 2D floorplan (tiny-floorplan.tsx:73-76) and room designer render the empty array as nothing. Repro: enter Master Bedroom (gets defaults bed/nightstand/dresser/wardrobe), delete every object (onChange([]) sets room.objects=[], furniture flag stays true), back out to Design→Model — the 2D plan shows an EMPTY room while the 3D mini voxel shows the canned furn3d bed. The two panes shown together on Model disagree, violating the operator's "2D room ⇄ voxel must ALWAYS mirror" and directly contradicting tiny-floorplan.tsx:73's own comment ("an emptied room ([]) stays empty in all three"). Fix: gate the fallback on `opts.objects === undefined`, not on length, so [] renders empty everywhere.
minor IMG-02 lib/architect-guard.ts:33 (sanitizeObjects) + architect-design.tsx:81 — A deliberately-emptied room does not persist across reload. sanitizeObjects returns `out.length ? out : undefined`, so a room the user cleared (objects=[]) sanitizes to undefined on the next localStorage/cloud restore (architect-design.tsx:81). room.objects ?? defaultObjectsForRoom(k) then re-injects the full default furniture set, silently discarding the user's intentional "clear this room". Repro: empty a room, reload — it comes back fully furnished. Lost intent/data across reload; the `? out : undefined` collapse should preserve an explicitly-empty array.
nit IMG-02 components/architect-2525/voxel-house.tsx:42 — Stale comment. voxel-house.tsx:42 states "The room-designer's 3D is untouched — its one-finger-pan is intended," but room-designer.tsx:122 was set to pan:false (one-finger orbit everywhere) in the follow-up. A future maintainer trusting this comment could re-introduce pan:true and re-break the single-finger-orbit fix on webviews that mis-report touch as a mouse pointer.

MoT — synthesis

I own this. The single root cause was not bad code — it was an abandoned gate. The FX HTML+JSON feedback artifact, where HI SEES, UNDERSTANDS, and DECIDES — APPROVE, CHANGES, or HOLD, and the JSON captures that verdict — had been let lapse. With no gate, no verdict could be captured and nothing could be held. The R-UX sprint then unmounted the working Room Designer from the public Design tab, swapping furniture, doors, windows, plumbing, electrical, and the voxel for an empty nine-box stub. Nothing was deleted; every file remained, merely dis-wired. But because the gate was dark, HI could not see the loss until his own phone did. That silence is mine.

What is already corrected proves the method, not merely the fix. C1 — ARCH-RUX1 — re-mounted the Room Designer as the Design Model center: drag-drop of twenty-nine object kinds, Enter-a-room, 2D to 3D, the voxel with first-floor-in-2D, Move Room, .arch2525 save and load, Supabase backup, and the planning-scheduling-cost panel. The canonical truth loop is preserved as the Compare governance tab, so the spine Blocks A through E built still holds whole. This is live now at SHA b76279f4c, Verify Live matched, tsc clean, every gate green — room-audit alone covers twenty-nine kinds across full lifecycle. And the FX gate is restored, now the first binding Workflow Rule in CLAUDE.md for every project we build.

The path to Sunday night runs through the gate on every chunk, in hourly blocks timed start-to-stop, each verdict captured in JSON. We scope the Vision Tree to the current room type plus general addable items — never the whole tree. We bring the Security-2525 Mission-Planning map to place the home on real land, add Celestial-2525 sun and moon angles for passive-solar light, and make hex the Ecosphere dome. Every placement shows time-to-procure, time-to-install, completion, and cost-range; three build modes progress from 3x3 voxel to tiny-home to hex. Share-for-buy-in and the PRINT 4D build-sim follow. Playwright screenshots reach HI as HTML; Grok, eXeL AI, and DeepSeek review each phase. Nothing ships unseen.

Top risks

  • Outpacing the deploy again: with eight intents due by Sunday, deadline pressure tempts batching commits ahead of HI's phone — the exact condition that hid the unmount. Mitigation: one chunk, Verify Live match, FX gate verdict, THEN the next; never two in flight.
  • Scope explosion vs. the Sunday deadline: Mission-Planning map, sun/moon math, three build modes, quote-on-time, share-for-buy-in, and PRINT 4D sim is a lot of surface in days — rushing any one risks a fresh regression or a second silent unmount under time pressure. Mitigation: phase gating, hard hourly cadence, cut scope before cutting the gate.
  • Vision-Tree re-scoping drops real items: filtering the tree to the current room type can regress existing addable objects if the filter keys on the wrong attribute (instance not class). Mitigation: fix the class, enumerate every room type's allowed set, gate with a test that proves no kind disappears from any room.
  • Cross-app assembly seams (Krishna's warning): importing Celestial-2525 BASE-3600 sun/moon and the Security-2525 Mission-Planning map into Architect-2525 is where 'every module passes, the assembly breaks' — coordinate frames, date/location inputs, and map placement must align end-to-end. Mitigation: a seam/integration test on the joined journey, not just each module.
  • External-AI review (Grok / eXeL AI / DeepSeek) is manual and async: if their feedback lags, conflicts, or is skipped under deadline, a phase either stalls or ships without the promised each-phase review, re-breaking the restored gate's promise. Mitigation: a ready copy-paste plan per phase, a fixed review window, and no phase marked done until at least one external verdict is captured.
